tldr_text:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio criticized the International Criminal Court during an address on Friday at the Federalist Society National Lawyers Convention in Washington, D.C. Rubio dismissed international law as a tool of global elites and warned the tribunal against enforcing rules that the United States does not recognize. He compared the United States rejecting the court to a Roman general commanding forces not to quote laws to men with swords. Independent and international outlets such as Truthout emphasized the separate submission by human rights advocates at the Hague calling for arrest warrants for President Donald Trump and Marco Rubio.

New York City officials are examining whether unapproved plans to expand a construction project contributed to the collapse of an adjacent apartment building on Bedford Avenue in Brooklyn. The building collapse on Bedford Avenue killed eight people, including two children aged 9 and 10, and injured 18 others. The Brooklyn District Attorney's Office launched a criminal investigation into the collapse. Records from the New York City Department of Buildings show the collapsed building had 98 open violations.

President Donald Trump has informed senior national security advisers in recent days that he may hold off on launching new military strikes against Iran if the United States faces no further provocations from Tehran or the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen. President Donald Trump launched a military conflict involving the United States and Israel against Iran in February. The United Nations reports that at least 25 seafarers have been killed in and around the Strait of Hormuz since the conflict began. Polling indicates that the war has incurred political costs for the Republican Party following the midterm elections.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth awarded the Joint Service Commendation Medal to Specialist Thomas Iglesias of the 3rd U.S. Infantry Regiment, known as the Old Guard, following an encounter at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier in Virginia. Video recorded on Veterans Day, November 11, showed the Army sentinel reprimanding Hegseth and his entourage after a member of the group talked and laughed on the monument's steps. The Pentagon stated that Hegseth welcomed the regiment to the Pentagon, where he presented the decoration. Representative Thomas Massie introduced articles of impeachment against Hegseth over the military conflict with Iran.

Demonstrators repeatedly interrupted House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries during a panel discussion at the What's Next Democratic conference in Denver, Colorado. While speaking alongside moderator Jessica Tarlov, Jeffries addressed party plans to reverse Medicaid cuts and extend Affordable Care Act tax credits when audience members shouted objections. Hecklers demanded action on Medicare for All and the Green New Deal, shouted for the impeachment of President Donald Trump, and labeled Jeffries a liar and a traitor. An online petition opposing Jeffries's bid for House Speaker accumulated over 1.1 million signatures.

SpaceX launched the 15th test flight of its megarocket system from its South Texas base, achieving orbit while failing in an attempt to catch the lower-stage booster. The flight lifted off at 4:47 p.m. local time, carrying 26 Starlink satellites into orbit. Following stage separation, the Super Heavy booster experienced a guidance, navigation and control issue near the end of its descent, prompting flight controllers to order a diversion to the Gulf of Mexico. The booster automatically diverted to the water after losing a single engine out of 33 during the burn phase.

U.S. Central Command confirmed that American forces intercepted two one-way attack drones launched by Iran toward Bahrain, resulting in no casualties or damage. The incident followed an official statement from Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claiming responsibility for destroying a U.S. early-warning radar system in Bahrain in retaliation for an alleged U.S. aerial strike on a telecommunications tower in Sirik, southern Iran. U.S. Central Command explicitly disputed the Iranian claim of a successful strike on the radar.

Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins won the Alaska gubernatorial election, becoming the first Democrat elected to the office since 1998. Kreiss-Tomkins defeated three Republican candidates on the ballot, including Bernadette Wilson, who received an endorsement from Donald Trump. The victory adds to a national midterm election wave that left Democrats controlling the governor's office in 30 states. Kreiss-Tomkins campaigned on increasing funding for public schools, lowering energy costs, and expanding data center infrastructure.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham faces intense political pushback over plans to reset the United Kingdom relationship with the European Union ahead of an upcoming summit in Brussels. Former Brexit negotiators and campaign figures, including Oliver Lewis and Michael Gove, launched a new grassroots campaign called Stay Out to oppose any realignment, warning that rejoining could cost billions annually. Concurrently, a Queen's University Belfast poll conducted by LucidTalk showed that more than half of surveyed voters in Northern Ireland favor rejoining the European Union.

Mohammed Alfatih, a former bodyguard to Hamas leader Ismail Haniyeh, was convicted at Birmingham Crown Court of unlawfully wounding an enforcement officer with a bladed weapon, possessing two knives, and causing criminal damage. Footage captured Alfatih chasing the vehicle with two large kitchen knives and half a brick, leaving the bailiff with a head injury requiring hospital treatment. During the trial, Alfatih argued self-defense and cited post-traumatic stress disorder. Alfatih arrived in the UK in 2014, received political asylum in 2015, and obtained British citizenship in 2020.

He defended past U.S. actions, including boat strikes in the Caribbean and the capture of Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro. He asserted that international law had been invoked against nearly every major foreign policy decision of the Trump administration.
B: That speech marked his first major remarks since Republicans suffered heavy defeats in the midterm elections earlier in the month. Rubio downplayed those election losses, urging conservatives to focus on long-term ideological influence rather than individual election cycles.

B: In New York City, officials are examining whether unapproved plans to expand a construction project contributed to the collapse of an adjacent apartment building on Bedford Avenue in Brooklyn. The developer sought approval for a nine-story structure featuring sixty-four apartments, a grocery store, and community space.
B: Buildings Department Commissioner Ahmed Tigani stated that the city had not approved the nine-story design. The developer, an entity tied to real estate investor Robert Fischman, was excavating the site when the neighboring structure gave way. The collapse killed eight people and injured eighteen others, including four firefighters. All eight deceased victims were born outside the United States, including three construction workers and two children from Colombia aged nine and ten.
A: The Brooklyn District Attorney's Office has opened a criminal inquiry into the incident. Department of Buildings records show the collapsed building had ninety-eight open violations. The agency lifted that stop-work order in May after the violation was addressed.
A: City Council Member Farah Louis stated that the collapse stemmed from systemic failures involving dozens of unresolved violations alongside an excavation site cited for defying city orders.

## OPINION | Party Leadership Must Answer For Structural Failures
A: This is Void Opinion. Through a progressive lens today. Party leadership must answer for structural failures.
A: Panel moderator Jessica Tarlov shared the stage while audience members shouted objections to party policy priorities. Security personnel escorted the shouting audience members from the hall after Jeffries responded by noting his upbringing in Brooklyn.
A: An online petition opposing the elevation of Jeffries to the position of House Speaker collected more than one million one hundred thousand signatures. Progressive critics spearheaded this mobilization against his leadership bid. No House Democrat launched a formal leadership challenge against Jeffries ahead of the upcoming caucus vote. Internal party discussions continue alongside activist efforts to draft Representative Ayanna Pressley for the speakership role.
A: We observe a widening chasm between institutional leadership and the foundational needs of the electorate. Democratic institutions exist to protect vulnerable populations from market volatility and systemic deprivation. When legislative strategies bypass universal healthcare expansion and ecological transformation, public frustration naturally spills into conference halls. The baseline demands for Medicare for All and the Green New Deal represent non-negotiable survival metrics for millions of citizens. We reject the proposition that incremental adjustments to tax credits and healthcare subsidies constitute adequate responses to systemic crises.
A: We recognize the argument that party unity remains paramount during periods of acute political opposition. Institutional loyalists contend that internal challenges weaken the collective front required to reverse Medicaid cuts and confront opposing administrations. We understand the strategic impulse to preserve organizational cohesion above all else.
A: Party cohesion built on the suppression of structural reform is an illusion. Cohesion requires shared purpose and genuine responsiveness to the constituencies that supply legislative majorities. When over one million individuals sign petitions opposing a leadership path, the party apparatus faces a structural referendum. We insist that genuine institutional strength emerges from confronting policy failures rather than silencing the voices demanding systemic equity. The upcoming caucus vote will test whether leadership chooses internal preservation over the material needs of the public.
